doc_name: Disappearance and murder of Gannon Stauch
text: Gannon Stauch (September 29, 2008 – January 27, 2020) was an American boy who was murdered by his stepmother, Letecia Hardin (then Stauch), in Colorado Springs, Colorado. His disappearance and death drew national attention and prompted a large-scale search effort involving multiple law enforcement agencies and volunteers. Gannon was reported missing by his stepmother on January 27, 2020, when she told the El Paso County Sheriff's Office that he had left home between 3:15 p.m. and 4 p.m. to walk to a friend's house but never returned. The initial press release described him as a "juvenile runaway," but three days later, the sheriff’s office reclassified the case as a missing or endangered person due to new information. The search involved thousands of hours of investigation and hundreds of public tips, with assistance from the FBI Child Abduction Rapid Deployment team, the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children, and the Colorado Springs Police Department. Search teams used drones, dogs, horses, helicopters, and divers to search various areas. Gannon's biological parents made emotional pleas for his safe return and thanked the community for their support. On March 2, 2020, Letecia Stauch was arrested in Myrtle Beach, South Carolina, on charges of first-degree murder of a child by a person in a position of trust, child abuse resulting in death, tampering with a deceased human body, and tampering with physical evidence. She was extradited to Colorado and held without bond at the El Paso County jail. According to the arrest affidavit released on May 5, 2020, Letecia Stauch killed Gannon in his bedroom on the day he went missing, stabbing him 18 times, hitting him in the head with an object, and shooting him with a handgun. She then cleaned up the crime scene and disposed of his body in a suitcase, lying to investigators about her whereabouts and activities. She claimed Gannon was sick and stayed home from school, and drove with him to various places, but surveillance footage showed she left home with Gannon in her truck around 10:15 a.m. and returned with him around 2:19 p.m. On March 17, 2020, Gannon's remains were found by a maintenance worker under Escambia Bay Bridge in Pace, Florida, more than 1,300 miles from his home. The cause of death was blunt force trauma, sharp force injuries, and a gunshot wound. Investigators believe Letecia Stauch transported his body to Florida by driving there in a rented van after initially dumping it in a remote location north of Colorado Springs and retrieving it later. Letecia Stauch pleaded not guilty by reason of insanity and claimed she had dissociative identity disorder due to childhood sexual abuse. She also accused her husband of being involved in Gannon's death, alleging he had connections to drug cartels and sex trafficking rings, but was found competent to stand trial by a state mental hospital and her claims were dismissed by the court as unfounded. Her five-week trial concluded on May 8, 2023, with the prosecution presenting testimonies from Gannon's father, Letecia's former employers, family, investigators, forensic experts, and state psychiatrists. The defense offered Dorothy Otnow Lewis, a controversial psychiatrist specializing in dissociative identity disorder, as their sole witness. The jury rejected both the insanity defense and Otnow Lewis' testimony, and Letecia Stauch was found guilty of all charges. On the same day, she was sentenced to life in prison without parole plus 156 years by Judge Gregory Werner, who described her actions as “the most horrific I have ever seen” and stated she deserved “the maximum sentence that I can impose according to Colorado law.”
